mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the Federal Funds Rate above 4% over the prior 3 months reduces the present value of expected future cash flows for equities, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by at least 0.25% over the past 3 months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during a similar 3-month rate rise period (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the 12-month change in CPIAUCSL exceeds +2%, the expected path of inflation for the next quarter increases, prompting investors to demand a higher risk premium on equities and thereby lowering S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: Inflation surprise remains below +2% for the subsequent quarter with SPX 60-day returns not statistically worse than during prior low-inflation periods (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden increase in monthly PAYEMS exceeding +10% suggests accelerating labor market strength, which raises wage growth expectations and pushes up equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 5-day forward returns.
failure_condition: No significant increase in wage growth is observed and SPX 5-day returns are not higher than during prior strong labor market episodes (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When GDPC1 (GDP) grows at a quarterly rate above +3% for two consecutive quarters, it indicates robust demand that supports corporate earnings expectations, resulting in positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 quarterly growth > +3% for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: Quarterly GDP growth remains below +3% and SPX 20-day returns are not higher than during comparable strong-demand quarters (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in INDPRO (Industrial Production) of more than 2% signals weakening manufacturing capacity, which reduces growth expectations and depresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: INDPRO recovers by +1.5% or more within the next month with SPX 60-day returns not statistically lower than during prior contraction periods (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent strength in both PAYEMS and UNRATE (unemployment) below 4% and 3%, respectively, indicates a tight labor market that supports wage growth and corporate hiring plans, driving positive S&P 500 20-day returns.
failure_condition: Either PAYEMS ≥ 4,000 or UNRATE ≥ 3% with SPX 20-day returns not positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of monetary easing (FEDFUNDS < 3%), the 5-day expected discount rate implied by SPX options tends to be lower than in tightening periods, supporting higher equity valuations and producing positive S&P 500 5-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: regime: FEDFUNDS < 3% for the past 3 months
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS rises above 3% in the next month with SPX 5-day returns not statistically higher than during prior easing periods (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the 6-month moving average of RSAFS (retail sales) falls by more than 5%, it reflects weakening consumer demand, which lowers growth forecasts and increases risk aversion, producing negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: RSAFS recovers by more than 5% over the next 6 months with SPX 20-day returns not statistically lower than during prior declines (p > 0.05).
